text:
maria: heads-up — running long-context perf-suite (100k tokens) and seeing steady mem growth on kvstore runner, looks like we leak ~2MB/min after ~30k tokens. thought it was batching, but traces point at the eviction window logic

sam: can you paste the failing run id and exact config?

maria: run id 2026-03-15-kv-longctx-17, config: `batch_size=8, max_seq=8192, kv_window=4096, slot_rotation=true`. repro loop attached. core log snippet: 

```
[INFO] kv: append @req=0x7fa3 token=1024 slot=4096 -> end=8199
[WARN] kv: eviction: candidate_start=4096 candidate_end=8199 evict_count=2048
[DEBUG] kv: reuse detected: slot=4096 last_request_id=6723 current_request_id=6724
```

maria: note `end=8199` — that +1 looks suspicious (should be inclusive end=8198). also seeing stale blocks served to new requests (cross-request contamination) after a rotate+evict cycle.

jin: this smells like an off-by-one in the eviction window calculation, especially if we compute `end = start + window` instead of `start + window - 1`. when we evict we might be keeping one extra token that shifts alignment for the next write.

ashok: we saw intermittent failing unit tests in `kv_reuse_tests` that would only repro under high token counts. i had a quick grep and found `end_index = start_index + window` in `kv_page.cc` around the rotation function.

perf-bot: [perf/regression] kvstore.memory.growth +12% in canary runs vs baseline (p95 latency unchanged).

nina: can anyone share a minimal patch? i can throw a unit test into the harness if we agree on the fix.

maria: minimal repro script: spin 16 requests with sequence lengths ~8192, alternate request ids, force rotation every N tokens. invariant we check: after rotation the slot's `request_id` must not change across allocations (no reused tag) unless explicitly recycled. currently we see `tag` reused with mismatched request_id.

sam: quick fix idea: make eviction compute inclusive end: `end = start + window - 1;` then ensure `for (i = start; i <= end; ++i)` semantics. also audit all callers for assumptions about inclusive/exclusive ranges.

jin: also check tombstone handling: if we tombstone an entry but keep its fingerprint in a neighboring slab due to rounding, the next append may read the stale fingerprint and treat as cache hit. add a stronger check: verify `request_id` on hit.

ashok: i tried a local patch swapping to `-1`, ran the unit harness for 10m tokens, no leak observed and cross-request reuse rate dropped to 0 in my run. i'll push a draft PR with the test logs.

nina: please include a regression test that runs in CI (fast mode) and a longci variant for nightly (to catch slow repro). also add a metric `kv.eviction.offbyone.detected` that increments when we see a reused slot with different request_id.

maria: agreed. also can we add an assert in debug builds: `assert(!slot.used || slot.request_id == current_request_id)` to catch this early in dev.

sam: for rollout: cherry-pick to `main` and `stable-2026-02`, enable canary on 5% of traffic for 24h with telemetry. after 24h and no spike, promote.

ashok: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1127 (draft) — includes patch, unit tests, and perf logs. still WIP on test flakiness.

maria: thanks ashok. i'll coordinate the canary and add the telemetry dashboard. once merged, i'll trigger a canary and keep an eye on `kv.eviction.offbyone.detected` and memory growth. :thumbsup:
